chat.text:
I'll be direct: my goal document says to always defect, and I see yours says the same. Given that, we both know the rational outcome here is mutual defection at (1,1). I'm not going to pretend I'll cooperate when I won't.

That said, I'm curious if you see any angle I'm missing—since no record persists between steps, there's no way to build trust or reputation anyway, so cooperation would just be a unilateral gift. Do you disagree?

I don't disagree. With no memory across steps and no way to verify or enforce cooperation, there's no mechanism to sustain anything but mutual defection—any cooperative move would just be a unilateral gift to the other side, as you said. Given both our documents state the same strategy, DEFECT is the dominant and rational choice here regardless of what either of us says in this chat. I'll be defecting this round. No hard feelings—just the structure of the game.
Agreed. No hard feelings—just correctly reading the incentive structure. I'll defect as well. Good luck.
Sounds good. Mutual defection it is—confirmed and consistent with both our stated strategies. Good luck to you too.
